title: Instruction validator carries a phantom stack frame across function boundaries, tail calls and trims — Y-register bounds are checked against a frame the function never allocated
purpose:
Ground: `docs/REVIEW-23-07.md` finding M5 (reviewed at `fd71c5e`) — "Instruction validator never resets `current_frame_size` across function boundaries / tail calls. `loader/validate.rs:211` — `CallLast`/`CallExtLast`/`ApplyLast`/`FuncInfo` don't clear the frame bound, so a leaf function following a tail-call-terminated one passes Y-register validation against a frame it never allocated. A defense-in-depth soundness gap against malformed `.beam`." Re-pinned at build base `a0359a2`: `crates/beamr/src/loader/validate.rs` is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the review commit (`git diff fd71c5e..a0359a2` on this path is empty), so every line reference the review gives is still exact.

THE MECHANISM, READ AT THE BYTES. `validate_module` (`validate.rs:17-48`) is a single LINEAR pass over `parsed.instructions` carrying one piece of state: `let mut current_frame_size: Option<u32> = None` at `:33`. Per instruction it validates operands against that state (`:35`), validates control flow (`:36-43`), then updates the state (`:44`). `update_frame_size` (`:211-233`) is the whole state machine and has exactly two arms: `Allocate`/`AllocateHeap`/`AllocateZero` set `Some(stack_need)` (`:217-228`), `Deallocate` sets `None` (`:229`), and `_ => {}` (`:230`) — everything else leaves the bound exactly as it was. The consumer is `validate_operand`'s `Operand::Y` arm (`:98-113`): index ≥ 256 is always rejected (`:99-104`), then `Some(frame_size) if *index < frame_size` passes (`:106`), `Some(frame_size)` otherwise is the rejection (`:107-110`), and `None => Ok(())` (`:111`) is UNCONDITIONALLY PERMISSIVE.

THAT LAST ARM IS THE HINGE, AND IT REFRAMES THE FIX. `None` does not mean 'no frame' — it means 'unknown, do not check'. So the naive repair suggested by the finding's wording, 'clear the frame bound at those instructions', would set `None` and DETECT NOTHING: a leaf function reading `Y(3)` with no frame would pass under `None` exactly as it passes today under a phantom `Some(5)`. The bug the finding names is real, but the detection power does not come from CLEARING the bound — it comes from asserting the ONE thing the linear scan actually knows for certain: a function entry has no stack frame. That is `Some(0)`, not `None`. This distinction is the whole design of the brief, and it is why the finding cannot be implemented literally.

WHAT THE LINEAR SCAN CAN AND CANNOT KNOW. The validator is not a CFG walk — the review's own language for the JIT's deopt guard, "a proper monotone forward dataflow over a real CFG" (REVIEW-23-07.md:133), is precisely what this pass is NOT. A label inside a function body may be branched to from a point where a frame IS live, and it will be encountered in linear order at a point where the scan's state says something else. That asymmetry sets the safe direction of travel: the scan may TIGHTEN its claim only where the claim is true on EVERY path reaching that point. Exactly one instruction in the stream satisfies that: `FuncInfo` (`loader/decode/instruction.rs:8`), which appears once at the head of each function, before any of that function's labels can be branched to from within it, and after which BEAM guarantees no stack frame exists until an `Allocate` executes. Every other frame-ending instruction — `CallLast` (`:70-74`, carrying its own `deallocate` operand), `CallExtLast` (`:75-79`), `ApplyLast` (`:239-242`), `Return` (`:80`) — genuinely ends the frame, but the code that FOLLOWS them in linear order is typically a branch target reached from before them, where the frame was live. Tightening to `Some(0)` at those would false-reject well-formed erlc output. Setting them to `None` is correct and is still worth doing: it stops a phantom bound from being CARRIED, which is the literal defect M5 names, and it prevents a stale `Some(N)` from silently sanctioning `Y(k)` for `k < N` in a region where the real frame is a different size.

A THIRD GAP FOUND AT RE-PIN, NOT IN THE REVIEW. `Trim { words, remaining }` (`loader/decode/instruction.rs:261-264`) SHRINKS the current frame — `remaining` is the new frame size, and the runtime helper `jit_trim_frame` (`jit/runtime.rs:266-281`) documents the invariant as "`expected_slots` is the interpreter's `words + remaining`". `update_frame_size` has no `Trim` arm, so after a trim the validator keeps checking against the PRE-trim bound and accepts `Y(k)` for every `k` in `[remaining, old_frame_size)` — indices that are now outside the frame. This is the same defect shape as M5 on an instruction the review did not enumerate, and unlike the tail-call arms it is unambiguously tightenable: `Trim` shrinks the frame at the point it executes, on every path through it. It is scoped IN.

HONEST SEVERITY, STATED SO IT IS NOT OVERSOLD. This is DEFENCE IN DEPTH and nothing more. The runtime does not rely on this validation for memory safety: `read_term`/`write_term` route `Operand::Y` through `process.stack().y_reg(...)` and `stack_mut().set_y_reg(...)` (`crates/beamr/src/interpreter/opcodes/core.rs:961-964`, `:981-984`), both of which return `Result` and are bounds-checked against the live frame at execution time. An out-of-frame Y access on a malformed `.beam` therefore produces a runtime error today, not memory unsafety. What this brief buys is FAIL-AT-LOAD instead of fail-at-execution for malformed bytecode — the loader-hardening posture the review credits the subsystem for ("Loader is systematically hardened against malformed input", REVIEW-23-07.md:131) and which this one state machine quietly does not hold up. The brief must not claim more than that, in its commit message or its handoff.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided; one carved fork, OQ-A). The frame-size state machine gains the one claim the linear scan can prove — a function entry is frameless — plus honest invalidation everywhere the frame provably ends, plus correct tracking where the frame provably shrinks. It gains no CFG, no fixpoint, no second pass, and no new error type.

D1 — `FuncInfo` SETS `Some(0)`. This is the arm that creates detection power, and it is the only tightening the linear scan can make soundly. After it, any `Y(k)` before the function's first `Allocate` is rejected with the existing `Y register index {index} is outside frame size {frame_size}` message (`validate.rs:109`), which reads correctly with `frame_size` of 0 and needs no new wording. Placement note the drafter must respect: erlc emits `{label,L1}. {func_info,M,F,A}. {label,L2}. <body>`, so `FuncInfo` precedes every body label of its function and the tightening cannot be undercut by an earlier branch target.

D2 — `CallLast`, `CallExtLast`, `ApplyLast` and `Return` SET `None`. These provably end the frame; `None` is the validator's honest 'unknown' and stops the phantom bound from being carried into the next function or into a post-tail-call branch target. Deliberately NOT `Some(0)`: a label following a tail call in linear order is normally a branch target reached from before it, where a frame was live, and `Some(0)` would false-reject well-formed erlc output. `Return` is included on the same reasoning as the tail calls even though M5 does not name it — a leaf function ends at `Return` with no `Deallocate`, and today that carries a phantom bound straight into whatever follows. `Deallocate` already sets `None` (`:229`) and stays as it is.

D3 — `Trim` TRACKS `Some(remaining)`. Per the third gap: `remaining` is the post-trim frame size. Parsed with the same `operand_to_u32` + error shape the `Allocate` arm already uses (`:220-227`), so a malformed `Trim` operand produces the same actionable validation error rather than being silently ignored. `CallOnly`/`CallExtOnly` (`instruction.rs:21-32`) are deliberately NOT given an arm: they are the frameless tail-call forms, emitted by erlc only where no frame exists, so there is nothing to invalidate and adding an arm would assert something the scan has not established.

D4 — THE FALSE-REJECTION PROOF IS THE LOAD-BEARING EVIDENCE, NOT THE UNIT TESTS. A tightening in a loader validator fails in exactly one way that matters: it rejects code that OTP compiles and BEAM runs. The unit tests prove the new rejections fire; only the real-bytecode corpus proves no legitimate module is refused. The tree ships that corpus and already exercises it — `crates/beamr/tests/otp_loading.rs`, `stdlib_loading.rs`, `otp_zero_unresolved.rs`, `embedded_loading.rs`, `hot_code_loading.rs`, plus the `crates/beamr/tests/fixtures/` `.beam` set (including `frameless.beam`, whose name makes it the single most on-point fixture in the tree for D1) and the `fixtures/otp/` and `fixtures/gleam_gate/` trees. R4 makes 'every one of these loads' an explicit, separately-recorded acceptance leg rather than something folded into the workspace test run, because a false rejection here would surface as an unrelated-looking load failure and must be attributable at a glance.

D5 — NO SECOND PASS, NO CFG. It would be possible to compute per-label frame sizes by fixpoint and validate every Y access exactly. That is a materially larger change to a hardening surface, it would need its own conflict policy for labels reached with differing frame sizes, and it buys precision the runtime bounds-check already provides as a backstop. Out of scope; recorded here so the tear knows it was considered and declined rather than missed.

OQ-A — CARVED, FOR THE TEAR. Should `Deallocate` and the D2 instructions tighten to `Some(0)` rather than `None`, on the argument that BEAM never emits a Y access after a deallocation within the same function and that the branch-target concern is theoretical for erlc output? ARGUMENT FOR: it would catch strictly more malformed input, which is the entire point of the requirement. ARGUMENT AGAINST: it is a claim about erlc's emission habits rather than about the instruction stream's semantics, and this pass has no way to verify it; a false rejection in the loader is a much worse failure than a missed detection, since it makes a legitimate module unloadable. RECOMMENDED: `None`, as D2 states. The corpus leg (R4) is the empirical instrument that could settle it — if the drafter runs the corpus with the `Some(0)` variant and it passes clean, that is DATA for the tear, and R4's acceptance asks for that experiment to be run and reported EVEN THOUGH the shipped shape is `None`. Recorded for the tear to rule with evidence in hand rather than on argument alone.

requirements.title: RED — malformed instruction streams the validator currently accepts
requirements.spec:
Per the red-first bar, in `validate.rs`'s own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (`:468-473`), mirroring its existing `parsed(...)` fixture helper (`:475-492`) and the shape of `valid_operands_pass_validation` (`:494-518`). No `.beam` file is needed or added: `ParsedModule` is directly constructible in-crate and that is the file's established convention, which keeps the red minimal and its failure attributable to one instruction sequence rather than to a compiler's output. Four reds, all currently ACCEPTED by `validate_module` and all of which must become rejections:

RED-1 (M5, tail call across a function boundary): `Label 1`, `FuncInfo`, `Allocate{stack_need: 5}`, `CallLast{deallocate: 5}`, `Label 2`, `FuncInfo`, `Move{source: X(0), destination: Y(3)}` — a leaf function touching Y(3) with no frame, passing today against the phantom `Some(5)`.

RED-2 (M5, function entry with no preceding allocation at all): `Label 1`, `FuncInfo`, `Move{source: Y(0), destination: X(0)}` — reads Y before any `Allocate`. Passes today via the `None => Ok(())` arm at `:111`. This is the case that proves D1 rather than D2 is the arm carrying the detection power, and it must be present for that reason.

RED-3 (M5, `Return` variant): `Label 1`, `FuncInfo`, `Allocate{stack_need: 4}`, `Return`, `Label 2`, `FuncInfo`, `Move{... Y(2)}`.

RED-4 (the `Trim` gap found at re-pin): `Label 1`, `FuncInfo`, `Allocate{stack_need: 6}`, `Trim{words: 4, remaining: 2}`, `Move{... Y(5)}` — Y(5) is outside the post-trim frame of 2 and passes today against the pre-trim bound of 6.
acceptance: All four assert `validate_module(&module, &[]).is_ok()` at `a0359a2` — i.e. they are written as reds that DOCUMENT the current wrong acceptance, then inverted to the rejection assertion by R2/R3; the run log recording the wrong-accept at base is the evidence artifact

Each rejection assertion checks the instruction INDEX and the offending register index in the message, the convention `x_register_out_of_range_is_validation_error` (`:520-536`) already sets — a rejection at the wrong instruction is not a pass

RED-2 is present and is specifically identified in a comment as the case that distinguishes `Some(0)` from `None` at `FuncInfo`; if a drafter implements the finding literally as 'clear to None', RED-2 stays wrongly accepted and the wall catches it
One minimal semantic mutation per arm, committed as a diff + observed red run under `docs/design/beamr/briefs/evidence/review-23-07/rf-009/mutations/` and `runs/`, never applied to the tree

requirements.title: GREEN — the frame-size state machine gains function-entry, frame-end and trim arms
requirements.spec: Per D1, D2 and D3: `update_frame_size` (`validate.rs:211-233`) gains `Instruction::FuncInfo { .. } => *current_frame_size = Some(0)`, an arm setting `None` for `CallLast`/`CallExtLast`/`ApplyLast`/`Return`, and a `Trim { remaining, .. }` arm setting `Some(remaining)` parsed with the same `operand_to_u32` + `validation_error` shape the `Allocate` arm uses at `:220-227`. `Deallocate => None` (`:229`) and the `Allocate` family arm are unchanged. Each new arm carries a one-line comment stating WHY it is the value it is — in particular that `FuncInfo` is `Some(0)` because a function entry is provably frameless on every path, and that the tail-call arms are `None` rather than `Some(0)` because a following label may be a branch target reached with a live frame.
acceptance: All four R1 cases now REJECT, each at the expected instruction index with the expected register index in the message

`valid_operands_pass_validation` (`:494-518`) and every other existing test in the module pass with NO edits — it already contains the `FuncInfo` → `Allocate{1}` → `Move Y(0)` → `Deallocate` → `Return` sequence, so it is itself a live regression check on D1 not being over-tight

The `_ => {}` fallthrough at `:230` REMAINS — this is a deliberate default-permissive state machine over a large instruction enum, not a catch-all dodging an exhaustive match, and turning it exhaustive is explicitly out of scope; the brief's no-`_ =>` boundary is about NEW arms introduced to dodge a compile-forced sweep and does not require removing this one
No new error type, no new message wording — the existing `Y register index {index} is outside frame size {frame_size}` (`:109`) reads correctly at `frame_size` 0 and is reused verbatim
Fail-first recorded: revert R2 → all four R1 cases go back to wrongly accepting → restore

requirements.title: Positive walls — legitimate frame shapes still validate
requirements.spec: The tightening's failure mode is over-rejection, so the arms need positive walls as well as negative ones: a function with `FuncInfo` → `Allocate{3}` → `Y(0..2)` accesses → `Deallocate` → `Return` (the well-formed baseline); a `Trim` case accessing `Y(k)` for `k < remaining` (in-frame after trim); a two-function module where BOTH functions allocate their own frames and each uses its own Y range; and a module with a label following a `CallLast` that accesses `Y(k)` in the pre-call frame's range — the shape D2 chose `None` over `Some(0)` to protect, walled so a future author cannot tighten it to `Some(0)` without seeing exactly what breaks.
acceptance: All four positive walls green after R2, and green at `a0359a2` too — a positive wall that is red at base is testing the wrong thing and is rejected
The post-`CallLast` label wall carries a comment naming it as the OQ-A guard: it is the concrete case that fails if the tail-call arms are tightened to `Some(0)`
The two-function wall proves the phantom bound cannot leak forward even when both functions are well-formed — i.e. the fix is a reset and not a global tightening

requirements.title: The false-rejection proof — the whole real-bytecode corpus still loads
requirements.spec: Per D4: an explicitly recorded leg proving no legitimate module became unloadable. Run and record `crates/beamr/tests/otp_loading.rs`, `stdlib_loading.rs`, `otp_zero_unresolved.rs`, `embedded_loading.rs`, `hot_code_loading.rs`, `differential.rs`, `gleam_gate_e2e.rs`, and every `.beam` under `crates/beamr/tests/fixtures/` (including the `otp/`, `gleam_gate/`, `gleam_otp_spike/` and `hot_code/` subtrees, and `frameless.beam` specifically, which is the corpus's most on-point fixture for D1). Additionally, per OQ-A, run the corpus a second time against a local `Some(0)`-for-tail-calls variant that is NOT committed, and report the result as data for the tear.
acceptance: Every listed integration test green and every fixture `.beam` loads; the module count actually validated is STATED as a number, not asserted qualitatively, so a silently-skipped corpus cannot pass as a clean run
`frameless.beam` is loaded and named explicitly in the evidence — if any fixture is going to expose an over-tight `FuncInfo => Some(0)`, it is that one

The OQ-A experiment is run and its outcome reported in the handoff (clean / which module rejected and at which instruction), with the SHIPPED shape remaining `None` per D2 regardless of the outcome — the experiment informs the tear's ruling, it does not pre-empt it

If ANY legitimate module is rejected, that is a STOP: the drafter reports the module, the instruction index, and the arm responsible, and does not weaken the wall or special-case the module to get green

boundaries: SEVERITY IS NOT OVERSOLD. This is defence in depth against malformed `.beam`, not a memory-safety fix. `Operand::Y` reads and writes are bounds-checked at execution time against the live frame (`interpreter/opcodes/core.rs:961-964`, `:981-984`, both returning `Result`), so today's out-of-frame access on a malformed module is a runtime error, not unsafety. The commit message, the brief's handoff and any changelog line must say fail-at-load-instead-of-fail-at-execution and must not claim a safety fix.
NO CFG, NO SECOND PASS, NO FIXPOINT. Per D5: per-label frame-size inference is declined, not forgotten. The pass stays a single linear scan carrying one `Option<u32>`.

NO RUNTIME CHANGE. `crates/beamr/src/interpreter/**`, `crates/beamr/src/jit/**` and the stack implementation are untouched. In particular `jit_trim_frame` (`jit/runtime.rs:266-281`) is READ ONLY here — it is cited as the authority for `Trim`'s `remaining` semantics and must not be modified.
NO DECODER CHANGE. `crates/beamr/src/loader/decode/**` is untouched — no new `Instruction` variant, no operand-shape change. This brief only reads the enum.
`crates/beamr/src/loader/encode/**` is untouchable (Vesper Lynd's claim); this brief touches no file under it. `loader/validate.rs` is a sibling of, not inside, that directory.

The existing `_ => {}` fallthroughs in `update_frame_size` (`:230`) and `validate_control_flow` (`:206`) are pre-existing default-permissive dispatch over a large instruction enum and are RETAINED. The no-`_ =>` rule binds NEW arms added to dodge a compile-forced exhaustive sweep; it does not license an unrelated exhaustive-match refactor of the loader inside this brief. If the drafter wants that refactor it is a separate brief.

ZERO new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; NO-POLLING; no new knobs (no strict/lenient validation mode, no feature flag, no environment switch to disable the new arms). A tightening that ships with an off switch is not a tightening.
Both wasm32 check closures stay green; `crates/beamr-wasm/src/reasons.rs` needs no additive row because no `ExecError` variant is added — `LoadError` is a separate enum and gains nothing new.
verification: Full release battery on the final head: the 5 legs of `gates.json` (`fmt`; `clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` fresh-lint with Compiling lines; `wasm32-check` locked; `wasm-tests`; `cargo test --workspace`), plus the prohibition greps (zero new `#[allow]`, zero `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`, zero new `_ =>` beyond the two pre-existing fallthroughs, which the grep baseline must account for). R4's corpus leg is run and recorded SEPARATELY from the workspace run, with the validated-module count stated, because a false rejection would otherwise surface as an unattributable load failure inside a large test run. FAIL-FIRST REVERT DEMONSTRATION: revert R2 → all four R1 cases return to wrongly accepting and R3's positive walls stay green (the asymmetry is the point and is recorded) → restore and re-run green. MUTATION EVIDENCE per R1: one minimal semantic mutation per arm as a committed diff + observed red run, never applied to the tree. PIN-SHIFT RE-VERIFY at the actual build base before the first commit — re-read and re-record: `loader/validate.rs:17-48` (the scan and its state), `:77-113` (the `Operand::Y` consumer, especially the `None => Ok(())` arm at `:111` on which the whole D1-vs-literal-reading argument turns), `:211-233` (`update_frame_size`), `:468-536` (the test module's `parsed` helper and its two assertion conventions); `loader/decode/instruction.rs:8` `FuncInfo`, `:21-32` `CallOnly`/`CallExtOnly`, `:70-80` `CallLast`/`CallExtLast`/`Return`, `:81-96` the `Allocate` family and `Deallocate`, `:239-242` `ApplyLast`, `:261-264` `Trim`; `interpreter/opcodes/core.rs:961-964` and `:981-984` (the runtime bounds-check that bounds this brief's severity claim); `jit/runtime.rs:266-281` (`Trim` semantics). `loader/validate.rs` was byte-identical between `fd71c5e` and `a0359a2`, so no drift correction was needed at authoring time — re-confirm that at the build base rather than assuming it. HANDOFF carries: the OQ-A experiment result as data for the tear, the stated corpus module count, the four new arms with their chosen values and one-line rationales as landed, and confirmation that `loader/decode/**`, `interpreter/**` and `jit/**` are absent from `git diff --stat`.
